question: The amount on a sum of ₹3,200 at 10% per annum compound interest, compounded annually, in 2 years will be:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The effective rate of compound interest for 2 years at 10% = 10% + 10% + (10 × 10) ÷ 100 = 21%.

Total amount after 2 years = Principal + Interest = 100% + 21% = 121% of Principal.

Amount = 121% of ₹3,200 = 1.21 × 3200 = ₹3,872.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,872.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹3,200

Rate of Interest (R) = 10% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T

**Calculations:**

⇒ A = 3200 × (1 + 10 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 3200 × (110 ÷ 100)²

⇒ A = 3200 × (11 ÷ 10) × (11 ÷ 10)

⇒ A = 3200 × 121 ÷ 100

⇒ A = 32 × 121

⇒ A = 3872

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3,872.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CI vs SI Difference for 2 Years

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years on a principal P at rate R% is directly calculated as D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Effective Rate Method

The effective compound interest rate for 2 successive years can be easily found using the successive percentage formula: Rₑff = R₁ + R₂ + (R₁ × R₂) ÷ 100.

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly instead of annually, the rate is halved (R ÷ 2) and the time period in terms of cycles is doubled (2T).
